A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Commander-GPT study. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, out-of-distribution experiments and routing analyses in Section 4.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results in Section 4, including Tables 2–4 and Figures 3–7.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same six specialist agents, learned or prompt-based routing, three commander families and result-integration procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate multimodal sarcasm detection on MMSD and MMSD 2.0 and retain the SemEval 2018 Task 3 out-of-distribution evaluation. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains fine-tuned BERT, Zero-shot CoT, Automatic Prompt Engineer, Plan-and-Solve, Generated Knowledge Prompting and S3 Agent. Comparator membership in Figure 5 and the case-study tables also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains the 19,816/2,410/2,409 training/validation/test splits for both MMSD datasets. Section 4.2 preserves the model configurations, training settings, inference-only treatment of LLMs and accuracy, precision, recall and F1 metrics.

E4.justification: Sections 4.5–4.10 retain identical component ablations, invocation-frequency analysis, out-of-distribution tests, subtask-count analysis, routing visualization and case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting for their original experiments. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 2 retains Commander-GPT F1 scores of 86.7/85.8 with BERT+ViT and 81.4/76.5 with GPT-4o on MMSD/MMSD 2.0. Ablations, plotted results and case-study predictions are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, subtask definitions, routing objective and integration equations (1–10) are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same modular-routing contribution, performance claims and generalization claims, including the abstract's 19.3% F1 improvement claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of commander capacity, agent complementarity and routing behavior are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning agent quality, dependence on labeled subtasks and computational cost.

D1.justification: Both retain the same hardware, software, hyperparameters, approximately 5,000 distilled routing-supervision instances and model-access links. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to monolithic multimodal models and earlier sarcasm-detection approaches.

P1.justification: V2 adds Prayag Tiwari to the author list with Halmstad University affiliation and contact information. The body prose, terminology and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 reflows the title page and body, moving Figure 2 from page 4 to page 5 and Figure 3 from page 11 to page 12. Other page breaks and spacing shift, while figure content, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds author information and changes typesetting and placement, while preserving the scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility details and limitations. These presentation changes produce no material improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
